This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 24.02.2023 passed in MACC No.370/2016 by the XXVIIt h Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Indore, whereby a total sum of Rs.1,08,973/- has been awarded to her by way of compensation.

sentences.text: 3. As per the appellant, on 19.04.2013 she was going along with her husband on a motorcycle from Astha to Indore.

When they reached Bilwani Culvert in Sonkach, respondent No.1, who was the owner and the driver of the offending vehicle, a motorcycle bearing registration number MP 09 ND 6072 and which was insured with respondent No.2, drove the same rashly and negligently and dashed the same against her motorcycle, as a result of which she fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
She was taken to the hospital for treatment where she remained under treatment for a considerable period of time.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9771 2 MA-4381-2023 4.
The appellant thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the claims tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.14,35,000/- to her by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.2 by filing its written statement.

Upon evaluation of the evidence Smt. Alakhnanda Makwana vs Sushil on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132048218/
1 brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.

sentences.text: 5. This appeal for enhancement of amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that her permanent disability which has been assessed by the claims tribunal at 6% is extremely low.

As a result of the accident, she had suffered permanent disability to the extent of 23%
but the same has illegally been taken only at 6% by the claims tribunal.
It is also submitted that the amount which has been awarded to the appellant for special diet, transportation and attendant is also extremely low.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per contra , learned counsel for respondent No.2/insurance company has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal to the appellant in which no interference is called for in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7.

I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
8.
In the accident the appellant held suffered fracture on her left knee and right hand.
Though she was operated upon but even then there has been a deviation of 10% and 20% respectively in both the limbs.
The doctor who had issued the permanent disability certificate of the appellant Doctor Ashish Jain was also examined before the tribunal and he had proved the same.

Looking to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9771 3 MA-4381-2023 overall injuries suffered by the appellant her permanent disability could not have been taken at 6% which deserves to be taken at 11%.
9. The amount which the appellant would be entitled for on account of permanent disablement would hence be Rs.4,000/- + 25% for future prospects of rise in income.
The same would be multiplied by 12 for making it annually.
The multiplier applicable would be 13.
The permanent disability is taken at 11%.
Thus under this head the appellant would be entitled for a total sum of Rs.85,800/-.
The amount awarded to the appellant for special diet, attendent and transportation is also low.
The same deserves to be awarded at Rs.10,000/- each.
10. The appellant is entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.1,71,973/- to her by way of compensation whereas the claims tribunal has erred in awarding her a sum of Rs.108973/- only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhancement in the award of compensation by Rs.63,000/- which shall be paid to her along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of payment.
11. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE jyoti Smt. Alakhnanda Makwana vs Sushil on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132048218/
